Collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey, this collection of 166 stone tools (2006,0315.1 - 166) were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey.

Collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station on his return from the East. title: Celt
provenance: Purchased from: Mark Peacey. Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.

Said to have been collected in western Nepal by Mr Walter Peacey (see Acq biography) during his military service in wartime India, these objects were nearly lost when he forgot the kit bag containing them at Leeds railway station, on his return from the East. They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.

They were returned to him a month later. They remained in his possession until his death in 1981 and have been sold to the Museum by his grandson, Mr Mark Peacey. The first part of this group (80 objects) came to the BM in January 2005 and is registered as 2005.1-13.1-80. The second part of this collection (234 objects) was found by the Peacey family in December of 2005 in another attic. It came to the BM in December 2005 as the final part of this large (ie now some 314 objects) collection.
